candidate_profile.description: The candidate correctly concludes that the company is gaining share in a shrinking market and losing margin through price pressure, then recommends cost reduction and diversification, though with moderate rather than exceptional synthesis.
behaviour_rules: Start with a clear recap and treat market share as a metric that requires context.
Use a workable profitability framework that checks both volume and price, along with cost trends.
Establish that costs are stable and therefore not the main source of declining profits.
Recognize that slight volume gains do not offset lower realized prices.
Identify competitor exits and shrinking market demand as signs of a structurally weakening industry.
Connect fresh-food preferences to lower demand for preservatives.
Conclude that the company has gained share mainly because the market is shrinking and weaker players have exited, while prices are under pressure.
Recommend focusing on cost reduction and diversifying into other chemicals with stronger demand.

expected_issues: Diagnosis is broadly correct but may not prioritize the causal chain especially sharply.
May mention cost reduction and diversification without fully exploring how to execute them.
Final synthesis may be good but not especially board-ready.
expected_feedback_points: Good recognition that market share can rise in a declining market.
Good elimination of cost inflation as the main issue.
Good diagnosis of price-driven margin erosion.
Correct explanation that competitor exits and lower demand are reshaping the industry.
Reasonable recommendation around cost reduction and portfolio diversification.
